Same as dump_msgpack(), but do not add MsgPack array header.

detaileddescription.para: Used by the legacy Tarantool 1.6 format.

memberdef.definition: void(* port_vtab::dump_lua) (struct port *port, struct lua_State *L, bool is_flat)
memberdef.name: dump_lua

briefdescription.para: Dump the content of a port to a given Lua stack.

detaileddescription.para: When is_flat == true is specified, the data is dumped directly to Lua stack, item-by-item. Otherwise, a result table is created. The is_flat == true mode follows Lua functions convention to pass arguments and return a results, while is_flat == false follows Tarantool's :select convention when the table of results is returned.

briefdescription.para: Dump a port content as a plain text into a buffer, allocated inside.

parameterdescription.para: Length of a result plain text.

briefdescription.para: Get the content of a port as a msgpack data.

detaileddescription.para: By an obsolete convention, C stored routines expect msgpack data as input format for its arguments. This API is also usefull to process a function returned value as msgpack data in memory. The lifecycle of the returned value is implementation-specific: it may either be returned directly from the port, in which case the data will stay alive as long as the port is alive, or it may be allocated on the fiber()->gc, in which case the caller is responsible for cleaning up.

briefdescription.para: Get the content of a port as a sequence of VDBE memory cells.

detaileddescription.para: This API is used to pass VDBE variables to user-defined Lua functions (see OP_Function in sql/vdbe.c). The lifecycle of the returned value is the same as for method, i.e. it depends on particular implementation

briefdescription.para: Destroy a port and release associated resources.
A single port represents a destination of any output.

detaileddescription.para: One such destination can be a Lua stack, or the binary protocol. An instance of a port is usually short lived, as it is created per request. Used to virtualize functions which can return directly into Lua or into network.
